theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Real Estate (+2.32%) and Materials (+1.48%) led the market today, while Technology (-1.73%) and Consumer Discretionary (+0.10%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -0.34% versus +0.77% for defensives and +1.04% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained +0.46% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -0.64%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -0.35%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 0.64% to 18.58, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 0.91% to $4,067.60, crude oil was little changed at $89.31, and bitcoin slipped 0.15% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
